title: Kennedy, Three Globalizations of Law and Legal Thought 1850–2000

53.title: Human rights and identity: what replaced rights and classes
53.text: HUMAN RIGHTS PLAY THE SAME ROLE IN CONTEMPORARY LEGAL CONSCIOUSNESS THAT 'PRIVATE RIGHTS' PLAYED IN CLT AND 'SOCIAL RIGHTS' IN THE SOCIAL. IDENTITY PLAYS THE ROLE PLAYED BY THE INDIVIDUAL IN CLT AND BY CLASSES AND NATIONAL MINORITIES IN THE SOCIAL. The contemporary ideal is a legal regime that is PLURALIST — but not in the CLT sense, which coordinated ATOMIZED INDIVIDUALS THROUGH UNIVERSALLY VALID ABSTRACT RULES, nor in the sense of the social, preoccupied with FINDING AND SUPPORTING THE 'VALID' 'LIVING' LAW OF SUBCOMMUNITIES as a route to distributive justice, BUT RATHER IN THE SENSE OF THE PROPER RECOGNITION AND MANAGEMENT OF 'DIFFERENCE'. The individual and corporate property and contract rights beloved of CLT were a LIMITED CLASS, hemmed in by the WORSHIP OF SOVEREIGN POWER on one side and the SHARP DISTINCTION BETWEEN LEGAL AND MORAL OBLIGATION on the other. THEY ARE THE ANCESTOR BUT NOT THE MODEL of contemporary human rights, nor are they central to their pantheon. The collective social rights (food, housing, work, health) beloved of the social have been more or less won in positive law, but, like the property rights of CLT, they are CONCEPTUALLY AT THE MARGIN of contemporary legal consciousness in its transnational form. Contemporary legal consciousness is the END POINT OF A LONG PROCESS IN WHICH THE GENERAL CONCEPT OF RIGHT ROSE FROM ITS HISTORIC LOW IN THE 1930s (the high point of both the right-wing and the left-wing versions of the social) TO BECOME A UNIVERSAL LEGAL LINGUISTIC UNIT. HUMAN RIGHTS ARE THE 'HYPOSTATIZATION' OF THIS TREND, FUNCTIONING AS UNIVERSALS, AT ONCE NATURAL AND POSITIVE, IN A WAY STRANGELY ANALOGOUS TO THE FUNCTIONING OF RIGHT, WILL AND FAULT IN THE PRIVATE LAW OF CLT. They also function sometimes as RULES (even absolute ones) and sometimes as MERE POLICIES, potentially relevant in virtually any legal dispute, even where no violation of an enacted constitution, charter or treaty is alleged.

cards.q: Which roles in contemporary legal consciousness correspond to the roles in CLT and the social?
cards.a: HUMAN RIGHTS play the role of 'PRIVATE RIGHTS' in CLT and 'SOCIAL RIGHTS' in the social. IDENTITY plays the role played by the INDIVIDUAL in CLT and by CLASSES AND NATIONAL MINORITIES in the social.

cards.q: In what sense is the contemporary ideal 'pluralist'?
cards.a: NOT in the CLT sense, which coordinated ATOMIZED INDIVIDUALS THROUGH UNIVERSALLY VALID ABSTRACT RULES; nor in the sense of the social, preoccupied with FINDING THE 'LIVING' LAW OF SUBCOMMUNITIES as a route to distributive justice. BUT RATHER IN THE SENSE OF THE PROPER RECOGNITION AND MANAGEMENT OF 'DIFFERENCE'.

cards.q: Are the property rights of CLT and the social rights the model for today's human rights?
cards.a: NO. The property and contract rights of CLT were a LIMITED CLASS hemmed in by the worship of sovereign power and the sharp legal/moral distinction — THEY ARE THE ANCESTOR BUT NOT THE MODEL and are not central to the pantheon. The collective social rights (food, housing, work, health) are won in positive law but CONCEPTUALLY AT THE MARGIN of contemporary transnational consciousness.

54.title: Identity as a lingua franca — in market law too
54.text: Contemporary legal consciousness organizes the bearers of claims according to their PLURAL, INTERSECTING 'IDENTITIES'. Identity represents at once an EXTENSION AND A COMPLETE TRANSFORMATION of the categories — social class and national minority — by which the social jurists broke up the Savignyan 'PEOPLE'. Contemporary identities intersect in the sense that EACH OF US HAS MANY OF THEM. In contemporary global legal consciousness the notion of identity is the DESCENDANT OF THE SOCIAL CONCERN NOT WITH DOMINANT BUT WITH SUBORDINATED OR DISCRIMINATED-AGAINST OR PERSECUTED IDENTITIES; identity is typically THE BASIS OF A CLAIM AGAINST THE 'MAJORITY' OR THE 'DOMINANT CULTURE'. Identity thinking ALTERNATES BETWEEN ESSENTIALIZING what it means to have a particular trait that sets its bearers apart — in order to develop and legitimate legal claims — AND TRYING TO RECONCILE THOSE CLAIMS WHEN THEY COLLIDE. Straightforward nationalist claims and claims based on class or national-minority oppression are no less frequent today than in the interwar period; THEY ARE JUST NO LONGER PARADIGMATIC. THE DISCOURSE OF IDENTITY AND RIGHTS looks at first sight like a public law and family law phenomenon, BUT IT IS IN FACT A GENUINE LINGUA FRANCA, JUST AS USABLE IN MARKET LAW. On the side of the typical beneficiaries — what the social jurists call the 'WEAKER PARTIES' (women, discriminated-against minorities, and today also 'the poor' understood as an identity rather than a class) — FORMAL MARKET LAW NO LONGER IGNORES IDENTITY: some public and private market actors, but not others, are forbidden to discriminate against some identities, but not others, which means that THEY MAY BE FORCED TO DEAL AGAINST THEIR WILL, at some economic cost, or forced to deal ON MORE FAVOURABLE TERMS THAN THE IDENTITY-BEARERS WOULD OBTAIN IN A 'FREE' MARKET. The history of discriminatory treatment of an identity grounds COMPLEX ECONOMIC CLAIMS against private market actors or owners in the present.

cards.q: What is the notion of identity descended from, and against whom is the claim usually made?
cards.a: It is the DESCENDANT OF THE SOCIAL CONCERN NOT WITH DOMINANT BUT WITH SUBORDINATED, DISCRIMINATED-AGAINST OR PERSECUTED IDENTITIES. Identity is typically THE BASIS OF A CLAIM AGAINST THE 'MAJORITY' OR THE 'DOMINANT CULTURE' — and identity thinking ALTERNATES BETWEEN ESSENTIALIZING the trait (to legitimate claims) AND TRYING TO RECONCILE THE CLAIMS WHEN THEY COLLIDE.

cards.q: How does the discourse of identity work in market law?
cards.a: It is a GENUINE LINGUA FRANCA, not merely a public law phenomenon. FORMAL MARKET LAW NO LONGER IGNORES IDENTITY: some actors are forbidden to discriminate against some identities, so THEY MAY BE FORCED TO DEAL AGAINST THEIR WILL at an economic cost, or to deal ON MORE FAVOURABLE TERMS THAN THE IDENTITY-BEARERS WOULD OBTAIN IN A 'FREE' MARKET.

55.title: The strong parties dress up as a minority
55.text: On the side of the 'STRONG PARTIES' — employers, creditors, sellers of tangible and intangible commodities — there is a persistent effort, EMBLEMATIC OF CONTEMPORARY LEGAL CONSCIOUSNESS, TO RECONFIGURE PROPERTY AND CONTRACT RIGHTS AS PARALLEL TO MINORITY IDENTITY AND ITS RIGHTS. THE EASTERN EUROPEAN DISSIDENT RIGHTS THEORISTS, for whom the social was implicated if not in communism then at least in tolerating it in the years up to 1989, INCLUDED PRIVATE PROPERTY IN THEIR CATALOGUE OF WHAT HAD BEEN DENIED UNDER COMMUNISM. The furthest realization of this trend is AMARTYA SEN AND HIS INCLUSION OF THE 'RIGHT TO ENGAGE IN ENTREPRENEURIAL ACTIVITY' IN THE CATALOGUE OF PROTECTIONS OF HUMAN CAPACITY, best understood perhaps as PART OF THE THIRD WORLD REACTION AGAINST THE SOCIAL as it manifested itself in the failed ISI regimes of the 1960s and 70s. THE INTERNATIONAL BUSINESS COMMUNITY has gradually adapted to the rise of identity-rights rhetoric by TURNING PROPERTY OWNERSHIP INTO A MINORITY IDENTITY AND GOVERNMENT REGULATION INTO THE ANALOGUE OF DISCRIMINATION BY LEGISLATIVE MAJORITIES. Through the WTO, for example, multinational firms demand protection of intellectual property rights against the practices of third world countries that refuse to recognize patents and trademarks or to prevent 'PIRACY' — and Kennedy cannot resist the remark: NICELY PARALLEL TO INTERNATIONAL CAPITAL'S DEMAND THAT THE IMPERIALIST STATES SUPPRESS TANGIBLE PIRACY IN THE MEDITERRANEAN IN THE EARLY 19TH CENTURY BY COLONIZING NORTH AFRICA. THE SOCIAL'S HOPE THAT AN INSTITUTIONAL MECHANISM BASED ON THE RECOGNITION OF ORGANIZED GROUPS (as in corporatism) COULD PROPERLY ACHIEVE RECONCILIATION HAS VANISHED. Just as the people/nation complex of CLT was torn apart by the focus on social classes and national minorities, SO THE ORDER BASED ON CLASSES AND NATIONAL MINORITIES SHATTERED WHEN THE NOTION OF IDENTITY BEGAN TO INTERSECT. The upshot: the notion of identity and the set of legal concepts and techniques based on the idea of right by which identities enter law (discrimination, accommodation and so on) ARE GENERAL — BUT THEY PROVIDE ONLY A LANGUE, USED TO MANUFACTURE AN INFINITE VARIETY OF PARTICULAR ARGUMENTS AND REGIMES OF POSITIVE LAW AS PAROLE. Each national legal system chooses for itself which identities to recognize and which to stigmatize, BUT THE ARGUMENTS FOR AND AGAINST RECOGNITION ARE ALMOST IDENTICAL ACROSS TIME AND SPACE. When an identity is recognized, it will typically be by the contemporary mixture of HIGHLY FORMAL NORMS OF EQUALITY AND NON-DISCRIMINATION with a highly negotiated, AD HOC set of norms about the TOLERATION OR ACCOMMODATION OF IDENTITY-DEFINING PRACTICES ('sodomy', the veil) and about AFFIRMATIVE ACTION OR REPARATIONS — in other words PUBLIC LAW NEOFORMALISM COMBINED WITH CONFLICTING CONSIDERATIONS. THERE WILL BE AS MANY SOLUTIONS AS THERE ARE LAW-MAKING AUTHORITIES.

cards.q: How did the strong parties adapt to the rhetoric of identity rights?
cards.a: They TURNED PROPERTY OWNERSHIP INTO A MINORITY IDENTITY AND GOVERNMENT REGULATION INTO THE ANALOGUE OF DISCRIMINATION BY LEGISLATIVE MAJORITIES. The Eastern European dissidents included PRIVATE PROPERTY in the catalogue of what communism denied; AMARTYA SEN included the 'RIGHT TO ENGAGE IN ENTREPRENEURIAL ACTIVITY' among the protections of human capacity; through the WTO firms demand protection of intellectual property against 'PIRACY'.

cards.q: Why did the social's hope of corporatist reconciliation vanish?
cards.a: Because just as the PEOPLE/NATION complex of CLT was torn apart by the focus on social classes and national minorities, SO THE ORDER BASED ON CLASSES AND NATIONAL MINORITIES SHATTERED WHEN THE NOTION OF IDENTITY BEGAN TO INTERSECT — each of us has many identities.

cards.q: What does legal recognition of an identity typically look like?
cards.a: A mixture of HIGHLY FORMAL NORMS OF EQUALITY AND NON-DISCRIMINATION with a highly negotiated, AD HOC set of norms about the TOLERATION OR ACCOMMODATION OF IDENTITY-DEFINING PRACTICES ('sodomy', the veil) and about AFFIRMATIVE ACTION OR REPARATIONS — that is, PUBLIC LAW NEOFORMALISM COMBINED WITH CONFLICTING CONSIDERATIONS. THERE WILL BE AS MANY SOLUTIONS AS THERE ARE LAW-MAKING AUTHORITIES.

56.title: The American genealogy of the third globalization
56.text: Every feature of the third globalization has a RECOGNIZABLE AMERICAN GENEALOGY, in the sense that working backwards from the present we soon run into American developments that at least prefigure the global ones. PUBLIC LAW NEOFORMALISM strongly recalls THE PRACTICES OF LATE 19TH-CENTURY AMERICAN COURTS, WHICH TOOK THE CLT CONSTRUCTION OF PRIVATE LAW AND APPLIED IT TO THE AMERICAN CONSTITUTION. After the Second World War the same practice was taken up, through the WARREN COURT, BY LIBERAL CIVIL LIBERTARIANS WHO HAD EARLIER SHARPLY CRITICIZED CONSERVATIVE PUBLIC LAW NEOFORMALISM. POLICY ANALYSIS AND BALANCING were a POST-REALIST American development, and the proponents of balancing were already debating the public law neoformalists IN THE EARLY 1950s. THE IDENTITY/RIGHTS COMPLEX is prefigured in the USA by the POST-WAR ALLIANCE OF ELITE WASPS, JEWS AND BLACKS IN CONSTRUCTING THE CATEGORY OF ETHNICITY, LINKING THE EVILS OF THE HOLOCAUST TO THE EVILS OF RACISM IN THE USA AS ILLEGAL DISCRIMINATION. AMERICAN SECOND-WAVE FEMINISM is responsible for the ABSTRACTION AND GENERALIZATION of that category by TURNING IT INTO 'IDENTITY'. And it has been known since DE TOCQUEVILLE that Americans incline towards JURISTOCRACY. THE MAIN SITES of the development of contemporary legal consciousness have strong American connections: (1) the CONSTITUTIONAL COURTS with judicial review, often concerning both the division of powers in federal systems and rights against the state, which have come into being all over the world since 1945; (2) the rise of TRANSNATIONAL JURISDICTIONS in many contexts from the EU through the WTO to the International War Crimes Tribunal; (3) in the practice of law, the development of the LARGE INTERNATIONAL AMERICAN-STYLE LAW FIRM and likewise of a globalized NON-PROFIT NGO SECTOR that understands itself as the 'INTERNATIONAL COMMUNITY' or 'INTERNATIONAL CIVIL SOCIETY'.

cards.q: What American genealogy does public law neoformalism have?
cards.a: It strongly recalls THE PRACTICES OF LATE 19TH-CENTURY AMERICAN COURTS, WHICH TOOK THE CLT CONSTRUCTION OF PRIVATE LAW AND APPLIED IT TO THE CONSTITUTION. After the war the same practice was taken up, through the WARREN COURT, BY LIBERAL CIVIL LIBERTARIANS — precisely those who had sharply criticized the earlier conservative neoformalism.

cards.q: Where did the identity/rights complex come from in the USA?
cards.a: From the POST-WAR ALLIANCE OF ELITE WASPS, JEWS AND BLACKS IN CONSTRUCTING THE CATEGORY OF ETHNICITY, which LINKED THE EVILS OF THE HOLOCAUST TO THE EVILS OF RACISM IN THE USA AS ILLEGAL DISCRIMINATION. AMERICAN SECOND-WAVE FEMINISM abstracted and generalized that category BY TURNING IT INTO 'IDENTITY'.

cards.q: What are the three main sites of the development of contemporary legal consciousness?
cards.a: 1) CONSTITUTIONAL COURTS with judicial review, arising all over the world since 1945. 2) TRANSNATIONAL JURISDICTIONS from the EU through the WTO to the International War Crimes Tribunal. 3) The LARGE INTERNATIONAL AMERICAN-STYLE LAW FIRM and the globalized NON-PROFIT NGO SECTOR understanding itself as 'international civil society'.

57.title: Is it 'really' Americanization? Imposition, bargaining, prestige
57.text: American influence is obvious, and as with the spread of CLT one can distinguish MORE OR LESS VIOLENT IMPOSITION from IMPOSITION THROUGH SUPERIOR BARGAINING POWER, and both from PRESTIGE. With the constitutional courts the development begins with the AMERICAN VICTORY OVER GERMANY, ITALY AND JAPAN IN THE SECOND WORLD WAR and continues with the VICTORY IN THE COLD WAR. Then there is the process in which USAID AND THE INTERNATIONAL FINANCIAL INSTITUTIONS BARGAIN WITH THIRD WORLD REGIMES DESPERATE FOR FINANCIAL RESCUE AND IMPOSE RULE-OF-LAW REFORM AS PART OF STRUCTURAL ADJUSTMENT. American courts have steadily extended their 'LONG ARM' JURISDICTION by the implicit threat that IF MULTINATIONAL DEFENDANTS REFUSE AMERICAN JURISDICTION, DEFAULT JUDGMENTS WILL MAKE ACCESS TO THE AMERICAN MARKET DIFFICULT OR IMPOSSIBLE. And Kennedy's analogy, worth knowing: THIS IS THE 19TH-CENTURY IMPERIAL BARGAINING WITH THE OTTOMAN EMPIRE OR CHINA OR EGYPT OVER LEGAL 'CAPITULATIONS' UNDER THE DOUBLE THREAT OF MILITARY INTERVENTION AND THE REFUSAL TO TRADE. ON THE OTHER HAND, IT IS EASY TO OVERSTATE THE EXTENT TO WHICH THE THIRD GLOBALIZATION IS 'REALLY' AMERICANIZATION. First, public law neoformalism and conflicting considerations have a EUROPEAN GENEALOGY as much as an American one — including, for policy analysis, RENÉ DEMOGUE AND PHILIPP HECK before the Second World War and the EARLY PROPORTIONALITY CASES OF THE GERMAN CONSTITUTIONAL COURT; KELSENIAN JUDICIAL REVIEW AND GERMAN ORDOLIBERALISM UNDERPIN PUBLIC LAW NEOFORMALISM. And as in the earlier cases there is a PROCESS OF CHOICE in which local elites around the world decide TO BE DOMINATED IN ONE WAY RATHER THAN ANOTHER. THE EUROPEAN COURT OF JUSTICE IS NEOFORMALIST IN INTERPRETING THE CANONICAL 'FREEDOMS' OF MOVEMENT OF GOODS AND PERSONS IN THE 'SINGLE MARKET' PARTLY — AS IS WIDELY ACKNOWLEDGED — IN ORDER TO CLOAK ITS LEGISLATIVE POWER IN THE MANTLE OF LEGAL NECESSITY.

cards.q: What does Kennedy compare American 'long arm' jurisdiction to?
cards.a: To 19TH-CENTURY IMPERIAL BARGAINING WITH THE OTTOMAN EMPIRE, CHINA OR EGYPT OVER LEGAL 'CAPITULATIONS' UNDER THE DOUBLE THREAT OF MILITARY INTERVENTION AND THE REFUSAL TO TRADE. Today the threat is that DEFAULT JUDGMENTS WILL MAKE FIRMS' ACCESS TO THE AMERICAN MARKET DIFFICULT.

cards.q: Why is the third globalization not simply Americanization?
cards.a: Because neoformalism and conflicting considerations also have a EUROPEAN GENEALOGY: for policy analysis DEMOGUE AND HECK before the war, the EARLY PROPORTIONALITY CASES OF THE GERMAN CONSTITUTIONAL COURT; KELSENIAN JUDICIAL REVIEW AND GERMAN ORDOLIBERALISM underpin neoformalism. And a PROCESS OF CHOICE operates — local elites decide TO BE DOMINATED IN ONE WAY RATHER THAN ANOTHER.

cards.q: Why is the European Court of Justice neoformalist?
cards.a: In interpreting the canonical 'FREEDOMS' OF MOVEMENT OF GOODS AND PERSONS IN THE 'SINGLE MARKET', partly — as is widely acknowledged — IN ORDER TO CLOAK ITS LEGISLATIVE POWER IN THE MANTLE OF LEGAL NECESSITY.

58.title: The constitutional courts of the periphery as mediators
58.text: Why is it that in a good many peripheral and semi-peripheral national legal systems the CONSTITUTIONAL COURTS established throughout the period — FROM THE LATE 1940s (INDIA) THROUGH THE 1970s (PORTUGAL, SPAIN, GREECE) TO THE 1990s (CENTRAL EUROPE, COLOMBIA, SOUTH AFRICA) — have acquired significant power and successfully annul legislative and executive acts? The background of AMERICAN MILITARY HEGEMONY, THE PRESSURES OF THE INTERNATIONAL FINANCIAL INSTITUTIONS AND WORLD CAPITAL MARKETS AND THE PRESTIGE OF AMERICAN INSTITUTIONS are parts of the story. BUT HERE TOO CHOICE SEEMS TO MATTER. Kennedy's reading: such a development of judicial power can be understood as A STRATEGY OF A PART OF THE LOCAL ELITE — THE PART WITH ACCESS TO JUDICIAL POWER AND LEGAL DISCOURSE — FOR DEALING BY MEDIATION WITH A CHARACTERISTIC SET OF CONFLICTING PRESSURES. In the economy these regimes were the sites of the elaboration of the institutions of the social, from LAND REFORM to ISI, by left- and right-wing nationalist regimes that came to power after the Second World War in the context of decolonization. SOMETIME IN THE LATE 1960s A RISING NEOLIBERALISM, WITH STRONG TIES TO CLT, BACKED BY THE REVIVAL OF RIGHT-WING POWER IN THE USA AND WESTERN EUROPE, BEGAN TO PRESS FOR THE DISMANTLING OF THE SOCIAL REGIMES, ESPECIALLY ISI. THIRD WORLD CONSTITUTIONAL COURTS MEDIATE BETWEEN THOSE PRESSURES AND THE RESISTANCE OF THE INTENDED BENEFICIARIES OF THE SOCIAL — PEASANTS, THE URBAN POOR, STATE EMPLOYEES AND BUSINESS INTERESTS WITH ACCESS TO THE RENTS GENERATED BY REGULATION. Sometimes the courts STRIKE DOWN social measures — THE GHANAIAN CONSTITUTIONAL COURT STRUCK DOWN THE COMPULSORY MARKETING COOPERATIVES OF LOCAL GIN PRODUCERS FROM THE NKRUMAH ERA. Sometimes they MITIGATE the impact of the neoliberal return — THE INDIAN COURT, WITH THE WARM APPROVAL OF DAVID BEATTY, POSTPONED THE EVICTION OF SQUATTERS FROM THE PUBLIC STREETS OF BOMBAY UNTIL THE MONSOON SEASON WAS OVER.

cards.q: How does Kennedy explain the power of constitutional courts in the periphery?
cards.a: As A STRATEGY OF A PART OF THE LOCAL ELITE — the part WITH ACCESS TO JUDICIAL POWER AND LEGAL DISCOURSE — FOR DEALING BY MEDIATION WITH CONFLICTING PRESSURES: between the NEOLIBERALISM pressing from the late 1960s for the dismantling of the social regimes and the RESISTANCE OF THE INTENDED BENEFICIARIES OF THE SOCIAL (peasants, the urban poor, state employees, businesses with access to rents).

cards.q: Give two examples of how the constitutional courts of the periphery mediate.
cards.a: THE GHANAIAN CONSTITUTIONAL COURT STRUCK DOWN THE COMPULSORY MARKETING COOPERATIVES OF LOCAL GIN PRODUCERS FROM THE NKRUMAH ERA (striking down a social measure). THE INDIAN COURT POSTPONED THE EVICTION OF SQUATTERS FROM THE STREETS OF BOMBAY UNTIL THE MONSOON WAS OVER (mitigating the neoliberal return).

cards.q: When were the constitutional courts of the periphery created?
cards.a: FROM THE LATE 1940s (INDIA), THROUGH THE 1970s (PORTUGAL, SPAIN, GREECE), TO THE 1990s (CENTRAL EUROPE, COLOMBIA, SOUTH AFRICA).

59.title: The reverse process in sex and the family — and what mediation means
59.text: A SIMILAR BUT REVERSED PROCESS operates in the areas of CIVIL LIBERTIES, SEX AND THE FAMILY. There the INTERNATIONAL PRESSURE COMES FROM INTERNATIONAL NON-GOVERNMENTAL ORGANIZATIONS pressing for the protection of political dissidents and for the liberalization of sexual and family legal codes. On the other side stand, often, THE ARMY AND TRADITIONALIST RELIGIOUS AND NATIONALIST ORGANIZATIONS. Again the constitutional discourses of PUBLIC LAW NEOFORMALISM AND PROPORTIONALITY allow the legally empowered part of the elite TO MEDIATE — according to the Egyptian court, 'CLITORIDECTOMY IS NOT SHARI'A, SO THE GOVERNMENT MAY PROHIBIT IT'. And now what mediation means: THAT NEITHER SIDE GETS EVERYTHING IT WANTS ON SOCIAL QUESTIONS, any more than the courts enact either the WASHINGTON CONSENSUS or the SOCIAL AGENDA. PUBLIC LAW NEOFORMALISM AND THE PROPORTIONALITY METHOD EMPOWER JUDICIAL INSTITUTIONS TO STAND ABOVE THE CONFLICT OF CLT-STYLE NEOLIBERALISM AND THE SURVIVING ELEMENTS OF THE LEFT SOCIAL, AND EQUALLY ABOVE THE CONFLICT BETWEEN LIBERALIZERS AND SOCIAL AUTHORITARIANS AND TRADITIONALISTS. THEY TAKE CONFLICTS OUT OF THE DOMAIN OF PURE POLITICS, WITH ALL ITS EXPLOSIVE POSSIBILITIES, AND MOVE THEM INTO THE DOMAIN OF LEGAL EXPERTISE, APPARENTLY UNDER SUPRA-POLITICAL LOCAL CONTROL. Kennedy adds that it will be a while before one can determine retrospectively what the CLASS BASIS of this mediating activity was. A first guess: the supporters of judicial review may have included LONG-ESTABLISHED COLONIAL OR PRE-COLONIAL COSMOPOLITAN ELITES, not wholly displaced or even strengthened by the social regimes, AND NEWLY ENRICHED GROUPS, oriented to a more cosmopolitan social stance and to the global market, who had managed to install themselves within the social dispensation. FOR THESE GROUPS THE PROPONENTS OF THE WASHINGTON CONSENSUS, THE LIBERALIZING NGOs, THE LOCAL ARMY, THE CULTURAL NATIONALISTS AND THE RELIGIOUS FUNDAMENTALISTS ARE ALL THREATS TO BE MANAGED AND ACCOMMODATED, BUT NOT ALLOWED TO SPOIL THE GOOD TIMES AND THE PROMISING FUTURE. The process of choice is possible because, as with the first two, THE THIRD GLOBALIZATION SPREADS A LANGUE AND PERMITS AN INFINITE VARIETY OF PAROLE TO THOSE WHO LEARN TO SPEAK PROPORTIONALITY, NEOFORMALISM, RIGHTS/IDENTITY AND JUDICIAL SUPREMACY. AS THE LANGUE SPREAD, IT LOST ITS DISTINCTIVELY AMERICAN QUALITY: American solutions begin to look like MERE PARTICULAR INSTANCES RATHER THAN PARADIGMATIC UTTERANCES. This is helped along by the PAROCHIALISM OF AMERICAN LEGAL CULTURE, which after the Second World War LOST THE OPENNESS TO THE REST OF THE WORLD THAT HAD BEEN ONE OF ITS REMARKABLE FEATURES WHEN AMERICANS WERE SELF-CONSCIOUS INHABITANTS OF THE PERIPHERY. If they want to influence the langue or claim ownership of its use, THEY MAY BE INEFFECTIVE, BECAUSE THEY KNOW IT IN ITS CONTEMPORARY TRANSNATIONAL FORM LESS WELL THAN THOSE WHO HAVE BEEN PURPOSEFULLY DEVELOPING IT ABROAD FOR THE LAST FIFTY YEARS.

cards.q: What does the mediation by constitutional courts mean, and what does it do to politics?
cards.a: THAT NEITHER SIDE GETS EVERYTHING IT WANTS — the courts enact neither the Washington Consensus nor the social agenda. Neoformalism and proportionality empower them TO STAND ABOVE THE CONFLICT and THEY TAKE CONFLICTS OUT OF THE DOMAIN OF PURE POLITICS, WITH ALL ITS EXPLOSIVE POSSIBILITIES, AND MOVE THEM INTO THE DOMAIN OF LEGAL EXPERTISE, APPARENTLY UNDER SUPRA-POLITICAL LOCAL CONTROL.

cards.q: Who, on Kennedy's guess, was the class basis of judicial review in the periphery?
cards.a: LONG-ESTABLISHED COLONIAL OR PRE-COLONIAL COSMOPOLITAN ELITES, not wholly displaced or even strengthened by the social regimes, AND NEWLY ENRICHED GROUPS oriented to the global market. For them the Washington Consensus, the liberalizing NGOs, the army, the cultural nationalists and the fundamentalists are ALL THREATS TO BE MANAGED AND ACCOMMODATED, BUT NOT ALLOWED TO SPOIL THE GOOD TIMES.

cards.q: Why may Americans be ineffective at influencing the contemporary legal langue?
cards.a: Because as the langue spread it LOST ITS DISTINCTIVELY AMERICAN QUALITY — and the PAROCHIALISM OF AMERICAN LEGAL CULTURE, which after the war LOST THE OPENNESS TO THE REST OF THE WORLD (that had adorned it while Americans were SELF-CONSCIOUS INHABITANTS OF THE PERIPHERY), means they KNOW IT LESS WELL THAN THOSE WHO HAVE BEEN DEVELOPING IT ABROAD FOR FIFTY YEARS.

60.title: The new problem: law and politics
60.text: The central position of the judge combines with the PROBLEMATIC STATUS OF JURISTIC METHOD AFTER THE CRITIQUES and with the MULTIPLICATION OF THE IDENTITIES of claiming parties to produce A NEW PROBLEM. And this is the most economical summary of all three globalizations the article offers: IN PLACE OF THE QUESTION HOW FAR LAW SHOULD BE MORAL (CLT) AND THE QUESTION OF THE RELATION BETWEEN LAW AND SOCIETY (THE SOCIAL), THE QUESTION IN CONTEMPORARY LEGAL CONSCIOUSNESS IS THE RELATION BETWEEN LAW AND POLITICS. THE JUDGE SIMULTANEOUSLY REPRESENTS LAW AGAINST LEGISLATIVE POLITICS AT HOME AND AGAINST SOVEREIGN POLITICS INTERNATIONALLY, AND MUST ANSWER THE CHARGE OF BEING A USURPER PRACTISING 'POLITICS BY OTHER MEANS'. Contemporary legal consciousness harbours a MULTITUDE OF NORMATIVE RECONSTRUCTION PROJECTS designed to overcome the opposition of CLT and the social and thereby to RESTORE THE RULE OF REASON IN LAW. It also harbours a multitude of METHODOLOGIES by which legal theorists try to achieve a detached understanding of law's relation to other domains. In place of, or alongside, the normative projects of CLT and the social — UTILITARIANISM, NATURAL RIGHTS, SOCIAL DARWINISM, CATHOLIC NATURAL LAW, MARXISM, PRAGMATISM, COMTEANISM — we have LEGAL PROCESS, LIBERAL RIGHTS THEORY (often mysteriously combined with ANALYTIC JURISPRUDENCE), EFFICIENCY ANALYSIS, REPUBLICANISM, COMMUNITARIANISM, LEGAL NEOPRAGMATISM, FEMINIST LEGAL THEORY, CRITICAL RACE THEORY. AND THAT IS ONLY THE AMERICAN COLLECTION. THERE IS NO MORE A DOMINANT RECONSTRUCTION PROJECT TODAY THAN THERE WAS A DOMINANT PHILOSOPHY OF LAW IN THE LATE 19TH CENTURY OR BETWEEN THE WORLD WARS. Among the INTERPRETIVE (as opposed to reconstructive) projects: analytic jurisprudence, the sociology of law, the economic analysis of law, the literary theorizing of law as text, the cultural study of law, CRITICAL LEGAL STUDIES, postmodern legal theory — and the interpretive modes ARE NO LESS VALUE-LADEN FOR HAVING GIVEN UP PRESCRIPTION. CRITICAL LEGAL STUDIES, THE APPROACH OF THIS ARTICLE, includes a CRITIQUE OF POLICY ANALYSIS FOR ITS PRETENSION TO EXCLUDE, THROUGH THE NOTION OF UNIVERSALIZABILITY, THE INESCAPABLE PARTICULARISM OF POLITICAL AND LEGAL CHOICE — and a CRITIQUE OF PUBLIC LAW NEOFORMALISM FOR SUPPRESSING THE MOMENT OF 'RULING' IN POLITICAL AND LEGAL CHOICE.

cards.q: What central question does each of the three globalizations have?
cards.a: CLT: HOW FAR LAW SHOULD BE MORAL. THE SOCIAL: THE RELATION BETWEEN LAW AND SOCIETY. CONTEMPORARY CONSCIOUSNESS: THE RELATION BETWEEN LAW AND POLITICS — the judge represents law against legislative politics at home and sovereign politics internationally and must answer the charge of being a USURPER PRACTISING 'POLITICS BY OTHER MEANS'.

cards.q: What does critical legal studies criticize in the two great post-war innovations?
cards.a: In POLICY ANALYSIS, its PRETENSION TO EXCLUDE, THROUGH THE NOTION OF UNIVERSALIZABILITY, THE INESCAPABLE PARTICULARISM OF POLITICAL AND LEGAL CHOICE. In PUBLIC LAW NEOFORMALISM, the SUPPRESSION OF THE MOMENT OF 'RULING' IN POLITICAL AND LEGAL CHOICE.

cards.q: Is there a dominant reconstruction project today?
cards.a: NO — no more than there was a dominant philosophy of law in the late 19th century or between the world wars. We have Legal Process, liberal rights theory, efficiency analysis, republicanism, communitarianism, legal neopragmatism, feminist legal theory, critical race theory — AND THAT IS ONLY THE AMERICAN COLLECTION.

61.title: Conclusion: law is politics by other means — and vice versa
61.text: THE LEFT AND RIGHT POLITICAL IDEOLOGIES PURSUED THROUGH CONTEMPORARY LEGAL CONSCIOUSNESS ARE NO MORE INTERNALLY COHERENT THAN THE LEGAL DOGMATICS OF CLT OR THE ORGANICIST DOGMATICS OF THE SOCIAL. This is, for Kennedy, AN IMPORTANT ANTIDOTE TO THE TENDENCY TO SEE THE DISCUSSION OF THE POLITICS OF LAW AS A REDUCTION OF LAW TO POLITICS. The reduction is impossible because THE PROJECTS OF THE RIGHT OSCILLATE BETWEEN LIBERTARIANISM AND SOCIAL CONSERVATISM; the projects of the left, for instance on the family law questions just discussed, BETWEEN A FEMINIST IDENTITY POLITICS OF PROTECTION AND A QUEER-THEORETICAL ANTI-IDENTITY POLITICS OF SEXUAL LIBERATION. In other words, THE CONTENT OF LEFT AND RIGHT PROJECTS IS NO MORE RELIABLY 'AXIOLOGICALLY DECIDABLE' (or 'determinate', as critical legal studies used to say) THAN THE PURE QUESTION OF LEGAL VALIDITY. If we follow the phenomenology of DECIDING UNDER UNCERTAINTY all the way to the choice of an interpretation of one's own politics, it turns out that there is a 'HERMENEUTIC CIRCLE': ONE'S COMMITMENTS AS AN ACTOR WITHIN LEGAL CONSCIOUSNESS SHAPE ONE'S POLITICS AS MUCH AS THE REVERSE. Even in CLAUSEWITZ's famous formulation, WAR IS POLITICS BY OTHER MEANS, NOT 'MERELY' POLITICS. In CARL SCHMITT'S REVERSAL of Clausewitz, POLITICS IS WAR BY OTHER MEANS, but it cannot be reduced to war: war as a 'means' may be an end, or a means to ends other than political ones. IF LAW IS POLITICS, IT IS AGAIN POLITICS BY OTHER MEANS, and much that is non-reductive can be said about those means. AND BY ANALOGY WITH SCHMITT IT ALSO SEEMS TRUE TO KENNEDY THAT POLITICS IS LAW BY OTHER MEANS — IN THE SENSE THAT POLITICS FLOWS AS MUCH FROM THE UNFULFILLABLE DEMAND FOR ETHICAL RATIONALITY IN THE WORLD AS FROM THE ECONOMIC INTERESTS OR SHEER LUST FOR POWER WITH WHICH IT IS SO OFTEN DISCURSIVELY ASSOCIATED. The narrative attempts to HISTORICIZE 'OUR' SITUATION, in the mode of LEFT CRITICAL THEORY COMBINED WITH MODERNISM AND POSTMODERNISM. THE THREE GLOBALIZATIONS ARE INCIDENTS IN A STORY OF MILITARY FORCE, ECONOMIC POWER AND IDEOLOGICAL HEGEMONY WITHIN THE CAPITALIST PERIOD OF WORLD HISTORY. But Kennedy does NOT understand that period AS THE PLAYING OUT OF THE LOGIC OF CAPITAL, BUT AS A PERIOD OF UNIVERSAL RATIONALIZATION PARADOXICALLY INTERTWINED WITH THE DEATH OF REASON. And the closing sentences, worth knowing: THE DEATH OF REASON PERMITS — BUT NEITHER REQUIRES NOR ITSELF BRINGS ABOUT — THE REAPPROPRIATION OF ALIENATED POWERS THAT CAN BE USED FOR LOCAL, NATIONAL OR TRANSNATIONAL CHANGE IN THE DIRECTION OF EQUALITY, COMMUNITY AND WILD RISKY PLAY. BUT THEY ARE POWERS WHOSE ETHICAL EXERCISE BEGINS WITH ACCEPTING THE EXISTENTIAL DILEMMAS OF UNDECIDABILITY THAT LEGAL DISCOURSE HAS RELENTLESSLY DENIED FROM GLOBALIZATION TO GLOBALIZATION.

terms.def: An actor's commitments within legal consciousness shape their politics just as much as their politics shapes their legal positions.

cards.q: Why can law not be reduced to politics?
cards.a: Because THE LEFT AND RIGHT IDEOLOGIES ARE NO MORE INTERNALLY COHERENT THAN THE DOGMATICS OF CLT OR THE SOCIAL: the projects of the right OSCILLATE BETWEEN LIBERTARIANISM AND SOCIAL CONSERVATISM, those of the left BETWEEN A FEMINIST IDENTITY POLITICS OF PROTECTION AND A QUEER-THEORETICAL ANTI-IDENTITY POLITICS OF SEXUAL LIBERATION. The content of left and right projects is no more reliably 'AXIOLOGICALLY DECIDABLE' than the pure question of legal validity.

cards.q: How does Kennedy use Clausewitz and Schmitt?
cards.a: In CLAUSEWITZ, WAR IS POLITICS BY OTHER MEANS, NOT 'MERELY' POLITICS; in SCHMITT'S REVERSAL, POLITICS IS WAR BY OTHER MEANS, but it cannot be reduced to war. IF LAW IS POLITICS, IT IS AGAIN POLITICS BY OTHER MEANS — and by analogy THE CONVERSE ALSO HOLDS, THAT POLITICS IS LAW BY OTHER MEANS, because it flows as much from the UNFULFILLABLE DEMAND FOR ETHICAL RATIONALITY IN THE WORLD as from economic interests or the lust for power.

cards.q: How does Kennedy understand the capitalist period, and how does the article end?
cards.a: NOT as THE PLAYING OUT OF THE LOGIC OF CAPITAL, but as A PERIOD OF UNIVERSAL RATIONALIZATION PARADOXICALLY INTERTWINED WITH THE DEATH OF REASON. That DEATH OF REASON PERMITS (but does not require) THE REAPPROPRIATION OF ALIENATED POWERS usable for CHANGE IN THE DIRECTION OF EQUALITY, COMMUNITY AND WILD RISKY PLAY — but THEIR ETHICAL EXERCISE BEGINS WITH ACCEPTING THE EXISTENTIAL DILEMMAS OF UNDECIDABILITY THAT LEGAL DISCOURSE HAS RELENTLESSLY DENIED FROM GLOBALIZATION TO GLOBALIZATION.

62.title: The table of the three globalizations — first half
62.text: Kennedy's TABLE 1 is the best study aid in the whole article. Row by row, CLT (1850–1914) / THE SOCIAL (1900–1968) / THE THIRD (1945–2000). RIGHTS: individual rights, property rights / group rights, social rights / HUMAN RIGHTS. EQUALITY: formal equality / social justice / NON-DISCRIMINATION. LEGAL IDEAL: liberty, system and legal science / solidarity, evolution and social science / DEMOCRACY, RIGHTS, THE RULE OF LAW AND PRAGMATISM. LEGAL CORE: private law / social law / CONSTITUTIONAL LAW. LEGAL PHILOSOPHY: legal positivism / legal pluralism / A MULTITUDE OF NORMATIVE RECONSTRUCTION PROJECTS. NORMATIVE IDEAS: right, will, fault / social welfare / HUMAN RIGHTS AND SOCIAL POLICIES. IDEA OF GOVERNANCE: the unitary state / corporatism / FEDERALISM. SOCIAL UNIT: the people / social classes, national minorities / PLURAL IDENTITIES. SOCIO-LEGAL UNIT: the nation state / institutions / CIVIL SOCIETY. THE BOUNDARY: law/morality / law/society / LAW/POLITICS.

cards.q: Using Kennedy's table, name the rights, equality and legal ideal of all three globalizations.
cards.a: RIGHTS: individual and property / group and social / HUMAN. EQUALITY: formal / social justice / NON-DISCRIMINATION. LEGAL IDEAL: liberty, system and legal science / solidarity, evolution and social science / DEMOCRACY, RIGHTS, THE RULE OF LAW AND PRAGMATISM.

cards.q: What is the legal core, the legal philosophy and the boundary in each globalization?
cards.a: CORE: private law / social law / CONSTITUTIONAL LAW. PHILOSOPHY: legal positivism / legal pluralism / A MULTITUDE OF NORMATIVE RECONSTRUCTION PROJECTS. BOUNDARY: law/morality / law/society / LAW/POLITICS.

cards.q: What is the social unit, the socio-legal unit and the idea of governance in each globalization?
cards.a: SOCIAL UNIT: the people / social classes and national minorities / PLURAL IDENTITIES. SOCIO-LEGAL UNIT: the nation state / institutions / CIVIL SOCIETY. IDEA OF GOVERNANCE: the unitary state / corporatism / FEDERALISM.

63.title: The table of the three globalizations — second half
63.text: TABLE 1 continued. LEGAL INSTRUMENT: the code / the special statute / THE CONSTITUTION, THE TREATY, THE CHARTER. LEGAL TECHNIQUE: deduction within a coherent and autonomous legal order / the rational development of law as a means to social ends / PUBLIC LAW NEOFORMALISM AND THE BALANCING OF CONFLICTING CONSIDERATIONS. LEGAL ACTOR: the law professor who drafts the code and expounds it / the legal sociologist, the legislator and the administrator / THE JUDGE (AND THE LITIGANTS). IMAGE OF THE ECONOMY: the free market / alternatives to the market / THE PRAGMATICALLY REGULATED MARKET. IMAGE OF THE FAMILY: patria potestas with unenforceable high moral duties / the family regulated in the interest of the state and society / THE LIBERAL FAMILY. PUBLIC INTERNATIONAL LAW: nation states, colonies and treaties / international institutions / INTERNATIONAL CIVIL SOCIETY, HUMAN RIGHTS AND ADJUDICATION. INTERNATIONAL ECONOMIC LAW: the gold standard, free trade, private international law / autarky, bilateralism, blocs, the IMF, the World Bank, GATT / THE EC, NAFTA, THE WTO, STRUCTURAL ADJUSTMENT. PRIVILEGED FIELDS: contract and commercial law / labour, administrative, family and international law / CONSTITUTIONAL, COMMERCIAL AND INTERNATIONAL LAW.

cards.q: What is the legal instrument, technique and actor in each of the globalizations?
cards.a: INSTRUMENT: THE CODE / THE SPECIAL STATUTE / THE CONSTITUTION, TREATY, CHARTER. TECHNIQUE: DEDUCTION within a coherent and autonomous order / THE RATIONAL DEVELOPMENT OF LAW AS A MEANS TO SOCIAL ENDS / PUBLIC LAW NEOFORMALISM AND THE BALANCING OF CONFLICTING CONSIDERATIONS. ACTOR: THE LAW PROFESSOR / THE LEGAL SOCIOLOGIST, LEGISLATOR AND ADMINISTRATOR / THE JUDGE (and the litigants).

cards.q: What is the image of the economy and of the family in each globalization?
cards.a: ECONOMY: THE FREE MARKET / ALTERNATIVES TO THE MARKET / THE PRAGMATICALLY REGULATED MARKET. FAMILY: PATRIA POTESTAS WITH UNENFORCEABLE HIGH MORAL DUTIES / THE FAMILY REGULATED IN THE INTEREST OF THE STATE AND SOCIETY / THE LIBERAL FAMILY.

cards.q: What does public and economic international law look like in each globalization?
cards.a: PUBLIC: nation states, colonies and treaties / INTERNATIONAL INSTITUTIONS / INTERNATIONAL CIVIL SOCIETY, HUMAN RIGHTS AND ADJUDICATION. ECONOMIC: the gold standard, free trade, private international law / AUTARKY, BILATERALISM, BLOCS, THE IMF, THE WORLD BANK, GATT / THE EC, NAFTA, THE WTO, STRUCTURAL ADJUSTMENT.

cards.q: Which fields of law are privileged in each globalization?
cards.a: CLT: CONTRACT AND COMMERCIAL LAW. THE SOCIAL: LABOUR, ADMINISTRATIVE, FAMILY AND INTERNATIONAL LAW. THE THIRD: CONSTITUTIONAL, COMMERCIAL AND INTERNATIONAL LAW.
